        ### Question
        Indicate which serum biochemical profile is suggestive of rickets due to vitamin D deficiency in a 5-month-old infant:

        ### Options
        opa. Normal calcium; normal phosphate; normal alkaline phosphatases (FA); normal parathyroid hormone (PTH); 25 OH vitamin D low.
opb. Normal calcium; low phosphate; Normal FA; Normal PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.
opc. Low calcium; high phosphate; FA elevated; Normal PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.
opd. Normal calcium; normal phosphate; FA elevated; Elevated PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "Vitamin D deficiency" -> "decreased intestinal absorption of calcium" -> "normal serum calcium levels maintained by parathyroid hormone" -> "normal phosphate levels due to renal conservation" -> "low 25 OH vitamin D" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Vitamin D deficiency" -> "increased parathyroid hormone secretion" -> "normal serum calcium due to compensatory mechanisms" -> "low phosphate due to renal excretion" -> "low 25 OH vitamin D" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Vitamin D deficiency" -> "increased alkaline phosphatase due to bone remodeling" -> "normal calcium levels maintained" -> "low phosphate due to renal handling" -> "low 25 OH vitamin D" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Vitamin D deficiency" -> "increased parathyroid hormone" -> "elevated alkaline phosphatase" -> "normal calcium and phosphate levels" -> "low 25 OH vitamin D" -> 90%

(Vitamin D Deficiency)-CAUSES/PREDISPOSES->(Complication)-ASSOCIATED_WITH->(calcium)
(Vitamin D Deficiency)-CAUSES/COMPLICATES->(loss; bone)-ASSOCIATED_WITH->(Alkaline Phosphatase)
